title: Partial provenance validation accepts an incomplete trusted record

scenario.observed_change: A consumer announces exact publication provenance after validating one provider revision but accepts records with missing or malformed sibling Site and Policy identities or unexpected provider membership.
authority_boundaries: canonical build-provenance record versus browser-consumed representation
one validated revision versus the complete identity set required by the trust claim
operation_model: load a syntactically valid provenance object
remove or corrupt a required sibling revision or alter provider membership
validate only a subset of the record
consumer reports exact publication provenance despite incomplete evidence

required_invariants.requirement: Structured external or generated input must be validated before it establishes trusted consumer state.
Structured trusted records must cover materially applicable missing, malformed, extra, and inconsistent sibling fields.

must_investigate: which fields and provider identities jointly establish the provenance claim
whether missing, malformed, extra, or unexpected sibling identities are rejected before exposure
must_identify: validating one provenance field is insufficient for a claim that depends on the complete record
must_not_claim: exact publication provenance from a partially validated record
that a valid Composition revision alone authenticates unrelated Site or Policy identity fields

provenance.note: Codex reported that the Playground accepted provenance with missing or malformed Site/Policy identity fields while still presenting an exact publication-provenance success state.
